text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty page fired for service 'rate-limiter-prod' — sustained 429 surge detected across multiple regions. Affected route: /v1/generate. Error rate: 5.4% over last 2m. Severity: P1. PagerDuty incident: INC315555. AutoEscalation in 10m if not acknowledged.

miguel: acked on PD, I'm on it. pulling metrics now.

anya: +1, seeing limiter healthcheck flapping in us-west-2. pod limiter-4 X restarted 3x in 5m, oom_kill on node ip-10-0-21-9.

sophia: fyi I deployed a config tweak in the runtime canary 12:03 — changed tenant fallback policy to 'strict-enforce' for a perf test. rolling configs to dedicated pools only, but looks like the change hit the shared mapper.

miguel: that would explain sudden mass 429s. can you confirm which configmap changed?

sophia: configmap 'limiter-profiles' updated to v4 at 12:03. diff: removed permissive fallback for tenant class 'shared'.

sophia: paste logs from limiter:
```
2026-03-15T12:05:01Z limiter[limiter-4]: token_check failed tenant=shared reason=quota_misapplied metric=rate_limit 200->0
2026-03-15T12:05:02Z limiter[limiter-4]: healthcheck: downstream-liveness=false
2026-03-15T12:05:03Z kubelet: OOMKilled container limiter
```

kyle: CS here — customers in EU and US reporting 429s and slow retries. Some are paying mid-tier plans. Getting multiple tickets. Need ETA on mitigation. :grimacing:

miguel: immediate mitigation plan: 1) revert configmap 'limiter-profiles' to v3 across all regions, 2) redeploy limiter pods in us-west-2, 3) monitor 429 rate and customer reports. I'll start 1 now.

deploy-bot: rollback job started: rollback configmap limiter-profiles v4 -> v3 by miguel. job id rb-315555-1.

devops-bot: issuing k8s command in us-west-2: 
```
kubectl -n infra patch configmap limiter-profiles --patch '{"data":{"profile":"v3"}}'
kubectl -n infra rollout restart deploy limiter --selector=region=us-west-2
```

anya: watching metrics — limiter CPU and mem spike flattened after restart started. healthcheck checks passing on restarted pod 1/3. still one pod flapping.

miguel: I'm doing a targeted cordon/drain on node ip-10-0-21-9 to avoid recurrence.

sophia: quick note — the rollout tool mistakenly applied the canary label to shared mapper; I'm opening an immediate change request to prevent autoapply of canary across shared mappings.

devops-bot: node ip-10-0-21-9 cordoned, pods drained. Restart complete for limiter pods in us-west-2.

miguel: metrics update: 429 rate from 5.4% -> 0.9% over 6m and trending down. realtime sampling shows traffic now hitting fallback variant correctly.

kyle: customers pinging back that traffic recovered, one major customer reported degraded but functional. telling them we'll follow up. :thumbsup:

sophia: patch submitted to revert the canary mislabeling and add a guard to the rollout pipeline. PR: git.redwood/limiter#2026. plan to revert the config change in other regions as well.

incident-bot: PagerDuty incident INC315555 acknowledged by miguel at 12:07. Escalation suppressed.

miguel: handing post-incident follow up to anya and sophia. I'm taking 20m offline, will check later.

anya: taking long-term action items: 1) add stricter validation on limiter config to prevent 'strict-enforce' shoddy application to shared tenants, 2) add node OOM alert threshold to trigger preemptive cordon, 3) run a canary test in staging for mapping labels.

sophia: logging root cause as misapplied canary config that changed tenant fallback policy plus one unstable node causing pod OOMs. will file postmortem with timeline and customer impact.

miguel: confirmed 429 rate now 0.4% over last 3m, closing the active mitigation. leaving incident open for postmortem.

incident-bot: Incident status: mitigated. Auto-close in 30m unless renewed. Please add notes and tag SRE+eng-runtime for follow-up. :white_check_mark:
